Where do we check that this isn't out of bounds of the underlying buffer?
Code has been refactored to avoid this.
Why is all this acceptable? What about handling of endianness? I feel that libpldm should be more helpful here.
Used libpldm's iterator macros to handle state effecter PDR.

Placement-new runs the constructor for the struct, which will initialize the struct members to their default values, overwriting the data. I don't think that's what you're after?

Consider using https://en.cppreference.com/cpp/memory/start_lifetime_as

It seems ```std::start_lifetime_as``` isn't available currently in OpenBMC CI as well as for Yocto openbmc (master branch) even after including ```#include <memory>```. 
Got this compilation error (same during local CI too):
```
../sources/pldm-1.0+git/host-bmc/host_pdr_handler.cpp:676:60: error: 'start_lifetime_as' is not a member of 'std'
|   676 |                             const auto* effecterPdr = std::start_lifetime_as<
|       |                                                            ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```
